title: TerraFlux energy offline inference onramp scratchpad
content:
Meeting 2025-11-03 (initial call with TerraFlux infra + product)
---
Attendees: Ava (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood), Maya (Redwood solutions), Jordan (TerraFlux infra), Priya (TerraFlux ML), Mateo (TerraFlux product)
Purpose: capture constraints for an air-gapped/offline deployment of Redwood Private for anomaly detection and short-horizon forecasting on distributed substation controllers. Customer wants a fully offline package (no outbound telemetry by default) and the ability to run on their existing GPU hosts in regional colocation spaces.

High-level ask from TerraFlux:
- Run Redwood inference runtime on-site in a sealed network (no internet egress).
- Support models up to ~70B parameters (they plan to use a fine-tuned open model).
- Latency SLO: 150-250ms p50 for 256-token streaming/generation workloads from edge gateways (hard requirement for some operator UIs).
- Throughput: burst to 32 concurrent requests per machine, sustained moderate traffic distributed across 4 sites.
- No outbound telemetry; audit logs acceptable via customer-managed syslog collector.
- Hardware: mixed fleet of 1x A30 and 2x A100 (40GB) nodes today; potential H100 upgrade in 12–18 months. Driver and CUDA constraints noted (RHEL 8.8, NVIDIA driver 525 currently).
- Security: KMS/HSM integration required for customer key ownership. FIPS-140 preference for HSM.
- Size constraint for offline bundle: installers + images < 400GB (they expressed concern about transfer size).

Notes / Gotchas (from conversation + follow-ups)
- Offline bundle: they expect a tarball of container images + a local registry bootstrap script, systemd unit files, and an installer that can run without Internet. Need to validate total size estimate. Suggest creating two artifact tiers: minimal (runtime + core models) and full (runtime + model catalog + tooling).
- Drivers/CUDA: current hosts on driver 525 (CUDA 11.8). Our current recommended runtime kernels target CUDA 12.x for H100 optimizations — must confirm backward compatibility for A100/A30 with our runtime; fallback kernels may accept slight perf regression. Engineering ask: validate runtime on driver 525 + CUDA 11.8 (test matrix).
- Quantization: Their model team wants int8 quantization to reduce memory footprint. Clarify which quantization toolchain we will support in air-gapped install (we cannot rely on cloud quantization service). Propose providing pre-quantized model artifacts in the offline bundle. Need to confirm licensing for quantization tools if third-party.
- KV-cache & prefix caching: offline env will still benefit, but local disk cache policies needed (configurable path, retention). Disk IO on their substation servers is limited — call out swap/ssd sizing.
- Telemetry & logs: they require no telemetry by default. We must provide an opt-in telemetry toggle in the installer and document what is collected. Also provide a script for exporting runtime metrics to a local Prometheus pushgateway or syslog.
- RPM vs container: customer ops prefers RPM/system packages for easier OS integration. Our standard private deploy is container-first; need to sketch an RPM installer wrapping the container runtime and local registry, or provide documented steps for their SREs.
- Kernel/Driver modules: some of their hosts are managed by third-party colo providers with strict maintenance windows; driver upgrades may not be trivial. Plan for runtime compatibility on their present driver version.
- HSM integration: they have Thales Luna/CloudHSM (vendor unclear). Need to capture endpoint/connector details. Also need to support KMS for model decryption keys and service identity keys.

Immediate action items (owners + rough ETA)
1) Runtime compatibility matrix (Liam) — validate Redwood runtime supports A30/A100 on NVIDIA driver 525 + CUDA 11.8; include perf delta vs recommended baseline. ETA: 2025-11-11.
2) Offline bundle sizing document (Ava) — propose minimal vs full artifact lists, estimate sizes, identify largest contributors (model files). ETA: 2025-11-07.
3) Quantization plan (Maya + Priya) — decide whether we provide pre-quantized artifacts or an air-gapped quantization tool. Confirm licensing implications. ETA: 2025-11-14.
4) Installer options note (Ava) — sketch two install flows: container tarball + local registry bootstrap, or RPM wrapper that deploys containers and systemd units. Include pros/cons. ETA: 2025-11-10.
5) Security/KMS discovery (Jordan + Redwood security POC) — capture HSM vendor, compliance needs (FIPS), key lifecycle requirements. ETA: 2025-11-06.
6) Follow-up call (all) — schedule week of 2025-11-17 to review compatibility results and sizing. (Ava to propose times)

Unresolved questions for TerraFlux (to confirm on next call)
- Exact HSM vendor and whether they will provide test endpoints for integration.
- Will they accept pre-quantized model artifacts or want to run quantization themselves?
- Are there strict egress/ingress rules for the local registry import (do we need to plan for physical transfer media only)?
- Minimum disk capacity per inference node (they mentioned 'limited SSD' — need numbers).
- Which telemetry/events they consider acceptable to forward to customer-provided syslog (we need list of fields).

Design considerations / suggested mitigations
- Provide a two-tier offline distribution: 1) Minimal runtime bundle (core runtime + small default model) ~ <40GB for quick staging; 2) Full model pack delivered on external drive or s3 package for transfer.
- Offer a pre-install checklist for colo ops: driver versions, GPU visibility tests (nvidia-smi output), required systemd units, firewall rules for local registry ports, and steps for importing the tarball.
- For quantization: recommend Redwood does quantization in-house (pre-quantized artifacts) to reduce customer ops burden — but block if licensing or IP concerns.
- Provide an explicit telemetry-off binary/config default and a signed compliance statement about no outbound telemetry when disabled.

Notes to self (internal)
- Coordinate with eng-serving-runtime to spin up a test cluster using a CUDA 11.8 base image and A100/A30 VMs to get empirical numbers.
- Check model store size estimates for common 70B LLaMA-like variants (full fp16 vs int8).
- Talk to security about offline KMS connector support and key wrapping flow (bring-your-own-key requirement).

Next steps (short term)
- Send follow-up email to TerraFlux with summary + ask for HSM vendor + disk capacity numbers (Ava) — by 2025-11-05.
- Internal RT standup: sync with runtime eng + packaging on compatibility test plan (Liam + Ava) — by 2025-11-06.

Quick links (placeholders to fill)
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TERRAFLUX-ONRAMP
- Slack thread: #terraflux-onramp (link above)
- Jira epic: TFRX-17

End of scratchpad.
summary: Initial TerraFlux onramp notes: air-gapped private deployment constraints, hardware & driver compatibility concerns, quantization delivery options, KMS/HSM requirements, offline bundle size considerations, and action items assigned to Redwood SE + eng.
